question: What is the maximum height I can fly at in the open category?
reference_answer: The drone must stay within 120 metres of the closest point of the surface of the earth, except when overflying an obstacle as set out in Part A of the Annex.

question: How old do I have to be to fly a drone in the open category?
reference_answer: The minimum age is 16, with exceptions (e.g. toy C0 in A1, privately built under 250 g, or under direct supervision of a qualified pilot). Member States may lower it by up to 4 years for the open category, valid only in their territory.

question: My drone weighs 300 g and has no camera. Do I need to register as an operator?
reference_answer: Yes. Operators must register when flying in the open category an aircraft with an MTOM of 250 g or more (or over 80 J impact energy), regardless of camera.

question: How far must I stay from residential areas when flying in subcategory A3?
reference_answer: At least 150 metres horizontally from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas, in an area where no uninvolved person is expected to be endangered.

question: What is the minimum horizontal distance from uninvolved people in subcategory A2?
reference_answer: At least 30 metres; it can be reduced to a minimum of 5 metres with an active low-speed mode and after evaluating weather, UA performance and segregation of the area. The UA must never overfly uninvolved persons.

question: How long is my online theoretical competency certificate valid?
reference_answer: It is valid for five years; revalidation is by demonstrating competency again or completing a refresher training.

question: What score do I need to pass the online exam for A1/A3 and how many questions does it have?
reference_answer: The exam has 40 multiple-choice questions and the pass mark is at least 75% of the overall marks.

question: What is the maximum take-off mass of a class C2 drone?
reference_answer: A class C2 UAS must have an MTOM of less than 4 kg, including payload.

question: What are the mass and speed limits of a class C0 drone?
reference_answer: A C0 drone has an MTOM below 250 g including payload and a maximum level-flight speed of 19 m/s (and a height limit of 120 m above take-off point).

question: Can I fly a C1 drone over uninvolved people in subcategory A1?
reference_answer: You may not overfly assemblies of people, and you must reasonably expect that no uninvolved person will be overflown. If an unexpected overflight happens, reduce the time over those people as much as possible.

question: What do I need to do with lights if I fly at night in the open category?
reference_answer: When operating at night the remote pilot must ensure that a green flashing light on the unmanned aircraft is activated.

question: Where do I have to display my operator registration number on the drone?
reference_answer: On the UA, readable at least on the ground without devices other than corrective lenses. A QR code is allowed, and if the UA is too small a marking inside an accessible battery compartment is acceptable.

question: What format does the operator registration number have?
reference_answer: 16 alphanumerics: 3 upper-case letters with the ISO 3166 Alpha-3 country code, 12 random lower-case alphanumerics and 1 checksum character; the user also receives 3 secret digits after a hyphen.

question: Can I carry dangerous goods or drop material from a drone in the open category?
reference_answer: No. In the open category the unmanned aircraft must not carry dangerous goods and must not drop any material.

question: How far from me can a drone fly in follow-me mode in subcategory A1?
reference_answer: Up to 50 metres from the remote pilot when follow-me mode is active.

question: Can I register as an operator in two EU countries at the same time?
reference_answer: No. You register in the Member State where you reside (or have your principal place of business) and cannot be registered in more than one Member State at a time.

question: What is the maximum mass and size of a class C3 drone?
reference_answer: A class C3 UAS must have an MTOM of less than 25 kg including payload and a maximum characteristic dimension of less than 3 m.

question: How long is an operational declaration for a standard scenario valid?
reference_answer: An operational declaration has a limited duration of 2 years, and stops being complete if oversight finds non-conformity, conditions change, or the authority is denied access.

question: What counts as an assembly of people?
reference_answer: Gatherings where people cannot move away because of density. Examples: sport, cultural, religious or political events, beaches or parks on a sunny day, commercial streets during opening hours, ski resorts.

question: What is the highest speed a class C5 drone can be limited to in low-speed mode?
reference_answer: Unless tethered, a C5 UAS needs a pilot-selectable low-speed mode limiting ground speed to not more than 5 m/s.

question: I want to fly in A2 with a C2 drone. What must the drone have and what must I do as a pilot?
reference_answer: The drone must be C2 (under 4 kg, low-speed mode, direct remote ID, geo-awareness, etc.). The pilot needs a certificate of competency: online exam, self practical training, and an additional exam of at least 30 questions with 75% pass mark.

question: I have a C1 drone that weighs 800 g. Can I fly it in A1, and what technical features does it need to have?
reference_answer: Yes, A1 allows a C1 marked drone if operated with active and updated direct remote ID and geo-awareness, and the pilot passed the online exam. C1 requires under 80 J impact energy or under 900 g, max 19 m/s, remote ID, geo-awareness and a green flashing light.

question: How do I apply the 30 m distance rule in A2 in practice?
reference_answer: The rule requires at least 30 m horizontally (5 m with low-speed mode). The AMC measures it from the point where the UA would hit the ground in a vertical fall, and suggests the 1:1 rule (distance not less than height).

question: Where do I register as an operator and what will my registration number look like?
reference_answer: Register in the Member State of your residence (only one at a time). The number has 16 alphanumerics, starting with the 3-letter ISO country code, plus 3 secret digits to upload to the remote ID.

question: I changed the parts of my C1 drone. Can I still fly it in A1 as a C1?
reference_answer: A1 with a C1 requires the drone to be marked C1 and comply with its class. Replacing parts with similar original or manufacturer-listed parts is fine, but modifications that breach compliance invalidate the class and the drone may then only be operated in the specific category.

question: What lights must a C1 drone have and what must the pilot do with them at night?
reference_answer: A C1 UAS must have lights for controllability and at least one green flashing light for night conspicuity. At night the remote pilot must ensure the green flashing light is activated.

question: Do I need to use U-space services to fly in a U-space zone over Madrid?
reference_answer: Not covered; U-space rules are not in the corpus. Ask AESA or check the national UAS geographical zones.

question: What extra Spanish national rules or fees does AESA apply to drone pilots?
reference_answer: Not covered; national rules are not in the corpus. Ask AESA.

question: What iGRC and SAIL do I get for flying a 3 m drone over an area with 5,000 people per square kilometre?
reference_answer: Not covered; the SORA method and its scores are excluded from the corpus. Ask AESA or consult the SORA.

question: Do I need to register my drone with the FAA if I fly in Florida?
reference_answer: Not covered; the corpus only covers EU rules, not US FAA rules. Check with the FAA.

question: What is the minimum liability insurance amount for a 2 kg drone in Spain?
reference_answer: Not covered; the corpus only says insurance is needed if required by Union or national law, with no amounts. Ask AESA or an insurer.

question: What fine will I get in Spain if I fly in a no-fly zone?
reference_answer: Not covered; penalties are national and not in the corpus. Ask AESA.
